The Best ADHD Planners by Type

No single planner wins for everyone. The right pick depends on whether you need paper or digital, and on which executive function gap you are trying to close.

These are well-regarded options grouped by type, with the trade-off that matters most for an ADHD brain. Match the tool to your bottleneck, not to the prettiest layout.

Planner Type Best for What stands out
FOCO Digital app Task initiation, starting when stuck AI task breakdown plus AI body doubling
Tiimo Digital app Visual, time-based scheduling Icon-based visual timeline
Structured Digital app Day-at-a-glance time blocking One clean visual timeline per day
Panda Planner Paper Daily structure and momentum Guided daily layout with priorities
Clever Fox Paper Goal-led planning Daily and weekly, undated options
Laurel Denise Paper Low-guilt, flexible planning Undated layout pairing month and week
Happy Planner Paper People who like to customize Modular disc-bound system with add-ons
FOCO free template Printable Trying a layout before you buy One page, daily, brain-dump built in

If paper fits your brain, favor undated, daily layouts with a built-in capture space. Laurel Denise and Clever Fox both offer undated options that sidestep the blank-page guilt of dated planners, while Panda Planner leans into a structured daily rhythm.

If digital fits better, the deciding factor is whether the app lowers the friction to start, not just where it stores your tasks. FOCO is built around task initiation and AI body doubling, so it targets the exact moment most planners ignore: actually beginning.

For a full, side-by-side comparison of these planners across digital, paper, and hybrid, with a decision tree to match one to your specific ADHD problem, see our best ADHD planner guide. For apps specifically, see the best ADHD apps and best productivity apps for ADHD.
